title: Schema Bridge: stream reconciliation + typed model mappers for Go SDK
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a ‘schema bridge’ layer in the Go SDK that makes it ergonomic to declare typed response structs for structured outputs, while reconciling streaming chunks and applying retry/backpressure semantics consistently. This ticket covers the API surface, generator helpers using Go generics, stream reassembly rules, and examples showing migration from untyped maps to schema-driven decoding for Redwood structured outputs.

Motivation: Teams using the Go SDK frequently need to parse streaming JSON envelopes into typed models, but current patterns either force users to buffer whole responses (bad for latency/RSV) or to write bespoke incremental decoders that are error-prone. We also need predictable retry semantics when the stream fails mid-response (resume vs restart trade-offs).

Scope:
- Define a small public API for declaring typed outputs and registering per-field validators.
- Provide a generic DecodeInto[T any](stream) helper that incrementally builds T from streaming JSON tokens.
- Implement stream reconciliation rules: idempotent chunk application, KV cache-aware prefix reuse, and clear semantics for partial commits on retries.
- Backpressure hooks so callers can signal slow down (channel-based), and runtime honors both SDK-level and server advisory pacing.
- Examples: chat completion streaming to a typed ChatMessage struct; embeddings + meta stream example; an example showing graceful restart with resume token.
acceptance_criteria: Public API: DecodeInto[T any](io.Reader, opts...) that accepts a schema descriptor and returns a streaming iterator of completed T values or a final aggregated T
Compatibility: Existing streaming helpers remain working; new helpers are opt-in and do not change default behavior
Retry semantics: documented policy for when we restart vs resume on ephemeral errors; SDK applies policy consistently in all examples
Benchmarks: end-to-end streaming latency overhead <= 5% vs raw json.Decoder baseline on representative payloads
Tests: unit tests for incremental decode, fuzz tests for chunk reordering, integration test with mock server to validate resume token behavior
design_notes:
High-level decisions and trade-offs: we favor a deterministic, idempotent application of streaming tokens to typed fields. For widely used patterns (chat tokens producing strings appended to a field) we expose a Concat policy; for array fields we expose Append/Replace policies.

Alternatives considered:
- Full AST buffer then unmarshal: simplest but defeats streaming benefits.
- Codegen-only approach: powerful but heavier UX and CI complexity. We settle on a hybrid: small generator for schema descriptors plus runtime generic helpers to keep ergonomics tight without requiring full codegen.

Resume semantics: the stream will include an optional resume_token in top-level envelopes. On transient network error we will attempt to reconnect and request from resume_token when provided. If no resume_token, and partial state policy is "fail-on-partial" we raise a retry error for application to decide; default policy is "restart-and-redeliver" for idempotent model outputs only.

Backpressure: provide a TokenWindow option and an SDK callback OnBackpressure(func(sentTokens int) BackpressureAction) so caller can opt out of aggressive buffering. Runtime applies a simple token bucket per-connection that the SDK can throttle against.
implementation_plan: Design API and write interface docs (this ticket) - owner: Diego
Prototype generic helper DecodeInto[T any] using json.Decoder incremental token reading - PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/462
Add schema descriptor generator CLI (internal) to create descriptors from struct tags - optional step for early adopters
Wire retry/resume logic with existing HTTP streaming layer and add resume_token handshake
Add backpressure hooks and expose TokenWindow option in client config
Add unit + fuzz tests, integration test with mock streaming server to exercise partial chunk delivery
Benchmarks, docs + code samples, and SDK changelog entry
tests: Unit: incremental decode of nested structs with Concat and Append field policies
Unit: failure modes when token is malformed mid-field (should return clear error with partial_state=true)
Fuzz: random chunk boundaries and ordering to ensure idempotent reassembly
Integration: mock server provides resume_token; client reconnects and resumes state without duplication
Bench: compare memory and latency to baseline json.Decoder approach using 1k, 8k, and 32k token payloads
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated behind 'schema_bridge' config in client options. Early beta to internal infra teams for 2 weeks, then invite 10 external teams via feature opt-in, collect feedback, iterate. After stability gates (no P0 regressions, <1% increase in error surface) flip default GA in go-sdk-2.4 release. Communicate migration guide and breaking changes (none expected) in SDK changelog.
